criteria.quote: Bellsprout Looks Fragile. Its Mouth Melts Iron.
criteria.revision: Hold back the iron detail in the title and open with the documented contradiction: "Bellsprout can't escape while rooted—but anything that moves gets an immediate vine attack." Reveal the iron-melting fluid later.

criteria.quote: It's barely seven-tenths of a meter tall and weighs four kilos.
criteria.revision: Remove the height and weight, which are not in the research. Replace them with specific Bellsprout behavior: "It traps and eats bugs, using its root feet to soak up moisture."

criteria.quote: How can something this skinny melt iron?
criteria.revision: Use an open question that the research can actually develop: "If Bellsprout can't escape while rooted, what happens when something moves?" Answer it first with its immediate vine attack, then reveal the corrosive fluid.

criteria.quote: Yet its thin, flexible body bends and sways away from attacks. / Then its mouth spits corrosive fluid that melts even iron. / But when its roots are planted, it can't escape an enemy.
criteria.revision: Reorder the evidence so the stakes build: establish that it is rooted and unable to escape, show that it immediately flings a vine at anything moving, then reveal that its mouth leaks fluid that melts even iron. Remove the unsupported size beat.

criteria.quote: This skinny flower can melt iron with its mouth. / Then its mouth spits corrosive fluid that melts even iron.
criteria.revision: The iron-melting fact is announced in the title, opening scene, premise, and payoff, so it cannot function as a reveal. Keep the opening focused on Bellsprout being unable to escape while rooted, and reserve "its mouth leaks a fluid that melts even iron" for the later reveal.

criteria.quote: This skinny flower can melt iron with its mouth. / It's barely seven-tenths of a meter tall and weighs four kilos. / Yet its thin, flexible body bends and sways away from attacks.
criteria.revision: Replace the repeated skinny/tiny framing with distinct research beats: root feet replenishing moisture, immediate vine attacks on anything that moves, inability to escape while rooted, and flexible movement that avoids attacks.

criteria.quote: Bellsprout is tiny and flexible, yet its mouth spits corrosive fluid that melts iron.
criteria.revision: Make the ending resolve the broader contradiction instead of repeating the premise: "Bellsprout can't escape while rooted, but it immediately attacks moving objects—and its mouth leaks fluid that melts even iron." Remove "tiny," which is unsupported by the research.

criteria.quote: Tiny body or iron-melting mouth—which shocks you more?
criteria.revision: Use a genuine choice between two documented traits: "Which is more unsettling: Bellsprout immediately flinging a vine at anything that moves, or its mouth fluid melting even iron?"
